resolutions.recommendation: Convert to the NETWORK row for this corridor: set PipelineNetworkGrouping='Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline' and CLEAR Status to blank (GEM's documented aggregate convention - see precedent rows below). Keep LengthKnownKm=1164 as the corridor summary. Do NOT delete the member segments. Also re-derive Capacity: 604 MMcf/d is both unit-inconsistent with the members (bcm/y) and smaller than every one of them, which cannot be right for a trunk.
resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Coastal trunk aggregate vs its four member segments
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster A: Coastal trunk aggregate vs its four member segments] P0483 (Mellitah Complex->Benghazi, 1164 km, 34in) is the aggregate of P1862 Brega-Benghazi (396) + P1863 Brega-Khoms (645) + P1864 Khoms-Tripoli (201) + P1865 Tripoli-Mellitah (158) = 1400 km. All five carry Status=operating today, so any status-filtered length total double-counts the corridor (1164 + 1400 = 2564 km of pipe recorded for ~1200-1400 km of physical asset). Capacity is separately incoherent: these are SERIES segments of one trunk, so capacity does not sum, yet P0483's 604 MMcf/d (~6.24 bcm/y) is LOWER than each member (10.76/11.61/17.05/16.99 bcm/y). Fix is structural, not a value edit. GEM precedent for a blank-Status network row with a PipelineNetworkGrouping label: P3656 Moomba Sydney Pipeline System (2081 km, blank), P3672 NSW Gas Network (blank), P3966 East-West Gas Pipeline + P5885 MGS III Gas Pipelines (both grouping='Master Gas System', blank), P7150 OQGN 2023 Full Schematic Map (4223 km, blank). 'n/a' is not a Status vocab value.

Needs Baird's ruling: retire as a digitization artifact, or re-scope/rename it if it is a genuine distinct spur.

resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster A: Coastal trunk aggregate vs its four member segments] Name ('Khoms-Melita' - note the non-standard 'Melita' spelling of Mellitah) describes the Khoms->Mellitah run, but the recorded 25 km is ~7% of that run's actual 359 km, at the same 34in diameter as the coastal trunk. resolutions.recommendation: CORRECT LengthKnownKm: 5246.00 is a decimal-shift error. The Wafa field is ~525 km from the Mellitah Complex; P6705 carries the correct 524.65. Propose LengthKnownKm=524.65 (or 525) pending Baird's confirmation. This is a live wrong value in the published tracker.
resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Wafa-Mellitah: a cross-tracker duplicate + a 10x length bug (sourced)
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster B: Wafa-Mellitah: a cross-tracker duplicate + a 10x length bug (sourced)] P0484 records 5246.00 km for a line whose own gem.wiki page, the operator (mellitahog.ly) and offshore-technology all put at ~525 km - an order-of-magnitude error, and 5246.00 vs 524.65 is a clean decimal shift. 5246 km would be longer than any pipeline in Libya by a factor of four. NOT flagged by the deep sweep's spec check, caught by arithmetic during cluster review. Independently, P0484 is confirmed REAL and correctly in GGIT: it is the 32in sales-gas trunk of the Western Libya Gas Project.

resolutions.recommendation: DELETE from GGIT - do NOT move to GOIT. The 16in Wafa-Mellitah line is oil/condensate, and GOIT ALREADY CARRIES IT as P0606 'Wafa-Mellitah Oil Pipeline' (operating, 525.00 km, 16.00in, Wadi Al-Shatii -> Mellitah Complex, sheet row 1939) - the same length and diameter as P6705's 524.65 km / 16in. Reclassifying P6705 into GOIT would create a duplicate there. Fold any refs P6705 carries into P0606 and drop the GGIT row.
resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Wafa-Mellitah: a cross-tracker duplicate + a 10x length bug (sourced)
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster B: Wafa-Mellitah: a cross-tracker duplicate + a 10x length bug (sourced)] RESOLVED WITH SOURCES (ref-sweep agent, 2026-07-28): six independent sources - Offshore Technology's separate gas and oil pages, and four Mellitah Oil & Gas pages - unanimously describe the Western Libya Gas Project's Wafa-Mellitah corridor as TWO parallel lines, 32in gas (P0484) and 16in oil/condensate (P6705). So P6705 is a real pipeline and not a duplicate OF P0484 - but it is a cross-tracker duplicate of GOIT P0606, verified against the 2026-07-28 GOIT snapshot. Keeping it in GGIT inflates Libya's gas count and km by a 525 km line that is not gas. SEPARATE, out-of-scope flag for the oil side: GOIT also holds P5215 'Wafa-Mellitah NGL Pipeline' (16in, same endpoints, row 1938) - P0606 vs P5215 may itself be a within-GOIT duplicate.

resolutions.recommendation: KEEP - the duplicate hypothesis against P6709 is refuted (see notes). But CORRECT LengthKnownKm: 32 km appears stale. Later OPEC editions put BOTH lines on this corridor at ~12 mi (~19.3 km), which is exactly the 19.31 km P6709 carries. Propose ~19.3 km pending Baird's confirmation. ALSO re-check Status: the Bouri Gas Utilisation Project (BGUP) targets first gas Sept 2026 and may add or replace same-diameter twin lines on this exact corridor - verify what is operating before the next publish.
resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Bouri-Bahr Assalam: a real twinned pair (sourced) - but the 4in is condensate
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster C: Bouri-Bahr Assalam: a real twinned pair (sourced) - but the 4in is condensate] RESOLVED WITH SOURCES (ref-sweep agent, 2026-07-28): OPEC ASB 2012, 2013 and 2017 consistently tabulate Bouri<->Bahr Essalam as TWO parallel lines, with ASB 2017 marking the entry explicitly '(2)' / '2 x 12 mi' / '4, 10 in'. Mellitah Oil & Gas's own 2019 Bouri Gas Upgrading Project tender independently specs '10" CS and 4" CS pipelines 20 km long' on the same route. So the near-identical names are two real assets, not one row entered twice under a misspelling - though P6709's 'Asslam' spelling should still be normalised or captured in OtherEnglishNames.

resolutions.recommendation: MOVE TO GOIT - this is the 4in CONDENSATE line, not gas. Unlike P6705 (cluster B) and P6713 (cluster D), GOIT does NOT already carry it: the 2026-07-28 GOIT snapshot has no Bouri or Bahr Assalam row among Libya's 57 oil rows. So this one is a genuine reclassification that creates a new GOIT row, not a delete. Confirm the GOIT check still holds at apply-time. Capacity is separately wrong - see the scm/y defect below; true value ~0.04 bcm/y.
resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Bouri-Bahr Assalam: a real twinned pair (sourced) - but the 4in is condensate
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster C: Bouri-Bahr Assalam: a real twinned pair (sourced) - but the 4in is condensate] RESOLVED WITH SOURCES - see P1859 for the twinned-pair evidence. The 4in of the pair is the condensate line. This is the THIRD condensate line found sitting in Libya's gas tracker in one batch (P6705, P6713, P6709), which is why the pattern is escalated as a class defect rather than three isolated fixes. Note the dispositions differ and must not be applied uniformly: two are deletes because GOIT already holds the asset, this one is a move because GOIT does not. ROOT CAUSE of the capacity figure: these come from OPEC ASB Table 4.10, whose column header reads '(1,000 scm/yr)'; the ingest took the raw cell and labelled it 'scm/yr', dropping the x1000. THE WORSE, SEPARATE DEFECT: 'scm/y' and 'scm/yr' are not units GGIT's CapacityBcm/y formula converts - all four Libya rows using them (P1858, P6709, P6713, P6714) compute CapacityBcm/y = 0.00 or blank and contribute ZERO to any Libya gas capacity total in the published tracker. Tracker-wide only 8 rows use this unit string: these 4 plus 4 Algeria rows (P6616, P6617, P6618, P6620), and all 8 read zero. Every other scm-family row in GGIT uses MMSCMD, which converts fine.

resolutions.recommendation: DELETE from GGIT - same disposition as P6705 in cluster B, and for the same reason. The 10in Sabratha->Mellitah line is CONDENSATE and GOIT ALREADY CARRIES IT as P6457 'Sabratha-Mellitah Condensate Pipeline' (operating, 107.00 km, 10in, sheet row 1765) against P6713's 109.00 km / 10in. Do not reclassify into GOIT - that would duplicate P6457. Fold any refs into P6457 and drop the GGIT row. Separately, Capacity=465166 scm/y is subject to the scm/y defect (see cluster C / P6709): true value ~0.47 bcm/y.
resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Bahr Assalam-Mellitah Pipeline 2: a condensate line GOIT already has (sourced)
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster D: Bahr Assalam-Mellitah Pipeline 2: a condensate line GOIT already has (sourced)] RESOLVED WITH SOURCES (ref-sweep agent, 2026-07-28): Offshore Technology and Offshore Magazine independently describe the Sabratha platform feeding Mellitah via exactly two lines - one 36in GAS line (= P1855) and one 10in CONDENSATE line. P6713 is that condensate line. This is the second instance of the identical failure mode in one country (P6705 in cluster B), which is why the pattern is escalated rather than filed as two isolated fixes: a condensate line gets entered in GGIT while GOIT already holds it, inflating the gas tracker's count and km. It also explains cluster D's original trigger - P1855 and P6713 sharing an exact 109.00 km is not a copy error, they are the two parallel lines of one riser bundle; only the tracker placement is wrong.

resolutions.recommendation: KEEP BOTH ROWS - the duplicate hypothesis is refuted (see notes). Two items remain on this row: (1) the scm/y capacity defect, see cluster C / P6709 - true value ~4.13 bcm/y; (2) verify the owner/operator split, which sources put at Mellitah Oil & Gas for THIS 34in line and Eni Oil for P6714's 10in line.
resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Bu-Attifel-Intesar: a real twinned pair, not a duplicate (sourced)
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster G: Bu-Attifel-Intesar: a real twinned pair, not a duplicate (sourced)] RESOLVED WITH SOURCES (ref-sweep agent, 2026-07-28): OPEC ASB 2013 (2012 data) and ASB 2017 (2016 data), both Wayback-recovered and read with pdftotext, independently list 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar' as TWO PARALLEL LINES on one 82 mi / 131.96 km corridor - a 34in operated by Mellitah Oil & Gas and a 10in operated by Eni Oil. Each table's capacity matches its GEM row EXACTLY (4,134,806 -> P1858; 258,425 -> P6714). So the identical 2-decimal length that raised the flag is the correct answer, not a copy error: twinned lines share a route. This also disposes of the competing gas+condensate reading floated when the cluster was opened - OPEC carries both lines in its GAS table, so the 10in is not the condensate analogue of clusters B and D. Do not merge.

resolutions.recommendation: KEEP - see P1858. Same two remaining items: the scm/y capacity defect (true value ~0.26 bcm/y) and the operator check (sources say Eni Oil for this 10in line).
resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Bu-Attifel-Intesar: a real twinned pair, not a duplicate (sourced)
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster G: Bu-Attifel-Intesar: a real twinned pair, not a duplicate (sourced)] See P1858. Noting explicitly for the reviewer: this row was opened as a suspected duplicate and closed as a real asset. The pattern that made it look like a duplicate - a large and a small line sharing a name and an exact length - is genuine twinning here, even though the same signature in clusters B and D did turn out to be a misplaced condensate line. The signature is a reason to look, not a verdict.

resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: NC-41 and E Structure: one Mellitah export corridor described twice
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster E: NC-41 and E Structure: one Mellitah export corridor described twice] P6708 (130 km, 30in, construction, StartYear 2025) and P6715 (130 km, 32in, construction, StartYear 2026) are both ~130 km 'X->Mellitah' gas lines out of the same NC-41 / Contract Area D concession, and sit at adjacent sheet rows (3988 and 3990). Identical length with differing diameter/start-year is the signature of two aggregator (GlobalData/offshore-technology) descriptions of one export corridor, not two parallel 130 km pipelines.

resolutions.recommendation: Paired with P6708 - see that row. Resolve as one cluster: keep one row, fold the other's name/refs in.

resolutions.redundancy_cluster_title: Nasser-Brega in both trackers: two real lines (sourced) - but a bad length
resolutions.researcher_notes: [cluster F: Nasser-Brega in both trackers: two real lines (sourced) - but a bad length] RESOLVED WITH SOURCES (ref-sweep agent, 2026-07-28): P1866 (gas) and GOIT P0599 (oil) are two genuinely separate physical lines on the same Nasser/Zelten-Brega corridor, not one asset double-entered. OPEC ASB 2012 lists them as distinct rows in SEPARATE tables (4.9 oil, 4.10 gas) with commodity-appropriate capacity units, and an independent 2014 incident report describes a 36in gas line commissioned 1970 rupturing at Km 18 - a real asset distinct from the 1961-built oil line. The length gap that raised the flag is therefore NOT evidence of a different, longer route: every source converges on ~172 km for the GAS line too, so 277 km is simply a wrong value. The redundancy question closes; the spec error stays open and is now the actionable item.
